newsitem.title: JAPAN: No pressure to change Japan credit rating - Moody's.
newsitem.headline: No pressure to change Japan credit rating - Moody's.

text.p: Moody's Investors Service said on Thursday that it does not see any immediate pressure to change Japan's sovereign credit rating.

Kenneth Pinkes, chief credit officer at Moody's, said that any country faces some degree of challenge, referring to such problems as the "jusen" mortgage firm mess in Japan, but added that these problems were offset by Japan's fundamental strengths.

"This is a country with enormous strength and I think... one has to balance the kind of issue we describe in the context of other fundamental strengths. I think it's our feeling that there are no immediate pressures on the sovereign rating of Japan," he said.
Japan is the only Asian nation which has a rating of AAA given by Moody's.
